newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end down, Telecom, Lion weakness resumes.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end down, Telecom, Lion weakness resumes.

text.p: * New Zealand share prices end weaker on heavy volume
293 -1 * NZSE-10 cap index -7.17 at 1,137.39 348 -8 * Volume NZ$98.6 million. Futures -6 at 1,144
New Zealand share prices ended weaker on Monday after one of the most active day's trade so far this year, again dominated by Telecom.
Telecom reversed Monday's gain to end 10 cents weaker at NZ$6.60 with trade in the stock representing about a third of the total turnover of NZ$98.6 million.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index, also undermined by an eight-cent fall in Lion Nathan to NZ$3.48, ended 7.88 points down at 2,300.48.
Brokers said that while the high volume in Telecom could be attributed to the company's share buyback programme, there was evidence of other large, unconnected trades going on.

"Clearly on the day there will be stock that was bought back by the company but there was stock crossed independently of that buyback, so one would suggest that there are people who believe there is a buy story in it," Campbell Stuart at SBC Warburg said. "Obviously there is a major seller too," he said.
Brewer Lion Nathan dropped eight cents to NZ$3.48 but on comparatively light volume.

Fletcher Energy mysteriously dropped 12 cents to NZ$3.83 on the eve of reporting its first half result. Analysts expect a net profit before abnormal items of just under NZ$100 million, up from NZ$20 million the same period a year ago.
While Telecom and Lion languished, Brierley Investments, coat-tailing its investment in British hotel group Thistle, continued its quiet advance, gaining three cents to close at NZ$1.39.
The forest products sector was largely holding its ground, Fletcher Paper easing one to NZ$2.93 and Carter Holt Harvey gaining one to $3.28.
